raw_content:
{
  "hook": "Marlborough's cool winds slap Wairau Valley Chardonnay vines awake every morning, and Oyster Bay bottles that electric jolt at $15. The wine is a stainless-steel sermon on citrus, no oak, no apology.",
  "wine_summary": "Oyster Bay pioneered stainless-steel Marlborough Chardonnay in the late 0s when the region was still a Sauvignon monoculture. They ferment 100% of the fruit in tank at 14-16 °C, capturing malic acid instead of softening it through malolactic, so the wine keeps the raw green-apple bite that mirrors the stony alluvial soils beneath the vines. The result is a unoaked Chardonnay that drinks like a Puligny without the price or the wood.",
  "terroir_expression": "Wairau Valley’s river-deposited greywacke and wind-blown loess over gravel-age gravel drain fast, forcing roots to struggle and concentrate acids; the cool maritime flow through the Richmond Range gap preserves those acids at night while the high UV daylight thickens skins for phenolic grip. In the glass that translates to lime zest, white peach skin and a wet-stone snap that disappears in oaked versions from the same valley.",
  "vinification_summary": "Whole-bunch pressed, cold-settled for 48 hours, then fermented in 100% stainless at 14-16 °C with an aromatic yeast strain (QA23) that amplifies grapefruit and green-peach notes; malolactic is deliberately blocked by chilling to 4 °C, keeping malic acid sharp and preventing the buttery diacetyl note that dominates most New World Chardonnay.",
  "food_pairing": "Nashville hot chicken — the laser acidity cuts cayenne oil and refreshes the palate. Fish-and-chip truck snapper with malt-vinegar shower — high acid mirrors vinegar, citrus notes echo lemon wedge. Fine-dining option: raw scallop crudo with yuzu and sea-grape — wine’s lime-zest top note dovetails with yuzu while its stony spine lifts the mollusk sweetness.",
  "comparable_wines": "Kim Crawford Unoaked Chardonnay — same stainless regimen and Marlborough source but slightly riper profile. Chablis Petit Chablis — same no-oak citrus-mineral axis, though Chablis has more chalk-derived tension. Santa Rita 120 Unoaked Chardonnay — similar price and tank style from Chile’s cooler Leyda blocks.",
  "style_profile": "Medium-bodied unoaked white with high acidity and citrus-green apple drive",
  "cellar_recommendation": "Drink within 3 years of vintage; screwcap keeps it fresh but the primary fruit fades fast. Stand upright in the fridge door, no need to decant.",
  "value_assessment": "$15–18 buys you unoaked Marlborough Chardonnay that out-acids most California Chardonnays at the same price. Kim Crawford and Santa Rita 120 sit beside it on the shelf, but Oyster Bay delivers sharper cut and better vintage consistency. Worth it if you want a clean, brisk white under twenty bucks.",
  "market_position": "You’ll find it on by-the-glass lists at casual bistros and in the cold box at big-box retailers — the wine supermarkets stock when they need a New Zealand white that isn’t Sauvignon Blanc. Collectors ignore it; week-night drinkers move cases.",
  "insider_take": "Most tasters confuse its blocked-malo snap with residual sugar — there’s none, just mouth-watering malic acid. Skip this if you need buttered toast in your Chardonnay; buy it when you want Chablis nerve at two-thirds the price.",
  "aging_potential_years": null,
  "drinking_window_min_years": 0,

}

parsed.wine_summary: Oyster Bay pioneered stainless-steel Marlborough Chardonnay in the late 0s when the region was still a Sauvignon monoculture. They ferment 100% of the fruit in tank at 14-16 °C, capturing malic acid instead of softening it through malolactic, so the wine keeps the raw green-apple bite that mirrors the stony alluvial soils beneath the vines. The result is a unoaked Chardonnay that drinks like a Puligny without the price or the wood.
parsed.terroir_expression: Wairau Valley’s river-deposited greywacke and wind-blown loess over gravel-age gravel drain fast, forcing roots to struggle and concentrate acids; the cool maritime flow through the Richmond Range gap preserves those acids at night while the high UV daylight thickens skins for phenolic grip. In the glass that translates to lime zest, white peach skin and a wet-stone snap that disappears in oaked versions from the same valley.
parsed.vinification_summary: Whole-bunch pressed, cold-settled for 48 hours, then fermented in 100% stainless at 14-16 °C with an aromatic yeast strain (QA23) that amplifies grapefruit and green-peach notes; malolactic is deliberately blocked by chilling to 4 °C, keeping malic acid sharp and preventing the buttery diacetyl note that dominates most New World Chardonnay.

Santa Rita 120 Unoaked Chardonnay — similar price and tank style from Chile’s cooler Leyda blocks.
parsed.style_profile: Medium-bodied unoaked white with high acidity and citrus-green apple drive
parsed.cellar_recommendation: Drink within 3 years of vintage; screwcap keeps it fresh but the primary fruit fades fast. Stand upright in the fridge door, no need to decant.
parsed.value_assessment: $15–18 buys you unoaked Marlborough Chardonnay that out-acids most California Chardonnays at the same price. Kim Crawford and Santa Rita 120 sit beside it on the shelf, but Oyster Bay delivers sharper cut and better vintage consistency. Worth it if you want a clean, brisk white under twenty bucks.
parsed.market_position: You’ll find it on by-the-glass lists at casual bistros and in the cold box at big-box retailers — the wine supermarkets stock when they need a New Zealand white that isn’t Sauvignon Blanc. Collectors ignore it; week-night drinkers move cases.
parsed.insider_take: Most tasters confuse its blocked-malo snap with residual sugar — there’s none, just mouth-watering malic acid. Skip this if you need buttered toast in your Chardonnay; buy it when you want Chablis nerve at two-thirds the price.
